fluff.overview: The Whirlwind-class destroyer entered service in 2606 as a product of Eaton Aerospace's comprehensive refit program at Inglesmond. Originally based on older Federated Suns destroyer hulls acquired by the Star League Defense Force following the Reunification War, the vessels were stripped to the frame and rebuilt with Terran Hegemony technology, transforming an aging escort design into a capable fleet combatant. The class earned its name from the superior maneuverability the refit imparted compared to the original hull, a quality that set the Whirlwind apart in fleet screening and pursuit operations. Armed primarily for engagements against other WarShips, the class mounted a heavy broadside battery that prompted many SLDF officers to regard it as a vessel that punched well above the destroyer classification. Despite its refit origins, the Whirlwind proved a sound design whose aggressive armament philosophy made it a respected opponent in fleet actions.
fluff.capabilities: At 520,000 tons and 610 meters, the Whirlwind is a destroyer designed primarily to engage other WarShips, devoting very little of its available weaponry to anti-aerospace fighter duties. The nose mounts four NAC/25 naval autocannons and a light naval gauss rifle for heavy forward firepower, supported by Artemis-guided LRM-20 racks and four extended-range large lasers. The forward quarters each carry a single light naval gauss rifle, leaving these arcs defended only by capital-grade weapons poorly suited to engaging small craft. The broadsides deliver formidable firepower with four NL45 naval lasers and a light naval PPC per side, supplemented by large pulse lasers and short-range missile batteries. Three NAC/35 naval autocannons anchor the aft battery. Five hundred and forty-five double heat sinks manage the thermal load. The Star League variant mounts 306 tons of improved ferro-aluminum armor, while the Clan refit nearly doubles protection to 459.5 tons of ferro-carbide. Two 65-meter gravity decks provide crew habitation. The vessel carries no docking collars and no escape pods, only ten life boats. The Clan refit adds a lithium-fusion battery for double-jump capability, a mobile HPG, ten aerospace fighters, and a Star of twenty-five Elementals, though the antique vessel's narrow corridors prevent the Elementals from using their battle armor within the ship.
fluff.deployment: The Clan Wolverine Weasel fought at the Battle of Barbados in June 2824, still operating with original Star League specifications before the later Clan refit. During the annihilation of Clan Wolverine by the Grand Fleet under ilKhan Nicholas Kerensky, the Weasel operated alongside the Vincent-class corvette Badger against Clan Snow Raven's Aegis-class cruiser Black Justice. When the Badger sustained critical damage to her jump drive, she deliberately overloaded her engines near the Snow Raven cruiser Avalanche, destroying herself while damaging the enemy vessel. The Weasel exploited the distraction to slip past the Avalanche and launch an attack on the transport WarShips carrying the assembled Clan ground forces.
fluff.history:
The Whirlwind-class destroyer originated from the Reunification War era, when First Lord Ian Cameron's Directive 22 of 2575 commanded each Star League member state to contribute military forces to the expeditionary force being assembled against the Periphery states. The Federated Suns contributed its Davion-class destroyers, and the SLDF leased twenty-two of these vessels for the war's duration. When the conflict ended, the SLDF purchased the remaining nineteen Davion Block I hulls and contracted Eaton Aerospace on Inglesmond to strip and rearm them with Terran Hegemony technology. The refitted vessels entered service in 2606, earning the name Whirlwind for their superior maneuverability.

A series of subsequent refits extended the class's operational life to just under 180 years, an impressive span for vessels built on pre-Star League hulls. The Whirlwind's design philosophy prioritized anti-WarShip engagements, with heavy forward and broadside batteries optimized for fleet actions rather than screening against fighters and small craft. This left certain firing arcs with limited point defense capability, a trade-off that concerned fleet commanders but one that the vessel's aggressive firepower generally compensated for in practice.

All surviving Whirlwinds departed the Inner Sphere with Kerensky's Exodus fleet. One vessel, the Weasel, fought at the Battle of Barbados in June 2824 during the annihilation of Clan Wolverine, the only documented Whirlwind engagement before the later Clan-wide refit program. In 2901, Clan engineers developed an upgraded variant that significantly improved armor protection, added double-jump capability, and incorporated fighter and infantry support capacity. The refit also installed communications equipment that extended the vessel's operational independence, though the ancient hull's narrow corridors imposed limitations on how embarked infantry could operate aboard.

Multiple Clans fielded Whirlwinds across the following centuries, including Ghost Bear, Steel Viper, Snow Raven, Jade Falcon, and Wolverine. The class saw action at engagements ranging from the Battle of Trafalgar during Operation SERPENT to the Wars of Reaving that consumed the Clan Homeworlds. Attrition took a steady toll through both conflicts. Clan Ghost Bear lost its Whirlwinds during the SERPENT campaign and its aftermath. Clan Steel Viper's pair were destroyed during the Wars of Reaving. At least one vessel changed hands multiple times before being destroyed during the Jihad. Clan Snow Raven proved the most enduring operator, maintaining Whirlwinds in active service through 3145 and making these ancient refit-origin destroyers among the longest-serving WarShip designs in known space.
